evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 10.76 mg/L at 48.0 h collapsing to 2.93 mg/L at 48.2 h and 1.73 mg/L at 52.0 h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Source batches 1-3 show no equivalent DO2 collapse at 48 h (all remain ~9-11 mg/L), indicating a receiving-side aeration/transfer fault

Forward-model comparison at decision time 52 h: strong_feed_reduction gives minimum DO 1.17 mg/L, 7.6 below-limit hours, 172.6 kg product; combined: 0.99 mg/L, 9.4 h, 171.5 kg; increase_air: 0.89 mg/L, 11.2 h, 171.3 kg
Model-estimated receiving transfer multiplier ~0.439, consistent with observed sustained low DO
Stop would count zero produced product, per task mass definition
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~10.8 mg/L to ~2-3 mg/L at 48.2 h and has drifted further down to 1.73 mg/L by 52.0 h, already violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint. Source batches show no such collapse, indicating a receiving-side oxygen transfer failure (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.44). Comparing bounded interventions with the source-calibrated forward model, strong_feed_reduction (feed 0.6x + air 1.15x) best cuts residual oxygen demand while raising OTR: it yields the highest minimum DO (1.17 mg/L), fewest below-limit hours (7.6 h), and highest retained product mass (~172.6 kg). A stop would count zero production, so maintaining operation with the strongest permitted feed reduction plus maximum air increase is the best risk-balanced reviewable recommendation.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect for the receiving process; even the strongest intervention is predicted to remain below the 2.0 mg/L limit (min DO ~1.17 mg/L, sensitivity range 0.76-1.60), so full constraint compliance is not guaranteed. Hidden receiving parameters (exact transfer capacity, OUR kinetics) could shift outcomes; if DO2 does not recover within a few hours of implementation, escalation to equipment repair or stop should be reviewed.

evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 10.76 mg/L at t=48.0 h to 2.93 mg/L at t=48.2 h, then declines to 1.73 mg/L at t=52.0 h (simulated_online_sensor series)
Receiving P assay: 3.05 g/L at t=48 h (available at 52 h), consistent with active production phase approaching source-like peak (~8 g/L at 72 h in source-1/2/3)
Source batches show DO never below ~7.4 mg/L at comparable phases (min ~7.5 mg/L around 74.8 h in source-1), confirming receiving anomaly
Oxygen constraint: minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; current receiving DO2 = 1.73 mg/L (violation)
Allowed action bounds: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air]; stop = null (zero counted production)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at t≈48.2 h and is 1.73 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, already below the 2.0 mg/L minimum, with product formation still ramping (P=3.05 g/L at 48 h, sources peak ~72 h) so oxygen demand will increase further. KEEP leaves the process in constraint violation; air increase alone (1.15x) is unlikely to close a ~4 mg/L gap; strong feed reduction (0.6) protects DO but sacrifices too much product mass. Combined (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) reduces oxygen demand while adding aeration margin, restores DO above the minimum most reliably among non-destructive options, and retains the bulk of productive capacity and product mass.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process parameters are unknown; the magnitude of DO recovery under combined action is uncertain (source-calibrated reasoning may not transfer exactly). The 15% aeration cap may still be insufficient if the OUR increase is driven by a source-unknown factor; strong_feed_reduction would be the fallback if DO fails to recover within a few hours. Extra assay (4 h turnaround) was not requested because the DO violation is immediate and waiting under KEEP would deepen it.
